- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — the live-spec push gate (SPEC M-6; scope grown by prover findings F7/F4;
# gate e added for INV-17, the prototype fence).
# Blocks a push unless every gate below passes.
#
# Generic pattern for a host project: copy this file, then in guardrails/README.md's
# "how a host adapts" section swap in your own test command and prover cadence — the
# gate shape (fresh review record / green tests / ownership / coverage) travels as-is.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"
GUARDRAILS="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails"

# -- deletion-only stand-down (SPEC INV-290, ROADMAP row 502) --
# git feeds this hook one ref-update line per pushed ref on stdin (githooks(5)); read it ONCE, here,
# before any gate below can touch stdin — a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and
# must never block on a read. A push whose every fed line deletes its remote counterpart (the
# all-zero local object id) carries no content for any gate to judge, so the whole chain stands down
# by name instead of falling to the reach map's conservative FULL — the fix for the 2026-07-27 hang
# (four tag deletions read as an empty diff, fell to the full suite, died on the two-minute limit).
# This check carries no gate letter: it is a triage read ahead of the chain, the placement
# check-push-reach.sh already holds inside gate b, not a net that blocks on red.
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  PUSH_REF_LINES=""
else
  PUSH_REF_LINES="$(cat)"
fi
export PUSH_REF_LINES
if [ -n "$PUSH_REF_LINES" ]; then
  set +e
  del_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-deletion-only-push.sh")"
  del_code=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$del_code" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "$del_out"
    echo "PUSH ALLOWED — deletion-only push: standing the full gate chain down (reason: a deletion carries no content for any gate to judge, SPEC INV-290); whatever would guard the deletion itself is unaffected, since no such gate exists in this chain today."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

fail=0

echo "== live-spec push gate =="

echo ""
echo "-- reach classification (one read, feeds gates a and b, SPEC INV-45) --"
set +e
reach_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-push-reach.sh")"
reach_code=$?
set -e
echo "$reach_out"

echo ""
echo "-- gate a: fresh prover record for today (one record per push: the re-check of the spec and the architecture, and the adversarial read of the pushed range, SPEC M-6/INV-116/INV-304) --"
# A prose-only or scoped diff (reach verdicts 0 and 2) never touches the spec, the architecture,
# or the matrix — the documents the prover record re-checks — so the record stands down by name
# on those two verdicts. Full reach (and every classifier failure, which falls to FULL) keeps
# the existing check unchanged.
case "$reach_code" in
  0)
    echo "   prose-only diff: the prover record stands down by name; full reach keeps the check."
    ;;
  2)
    echo "   scoped infra diff: the prover record stands down by name; full reach keeps the check."
    ;;
  *)
    if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prover-record.sh" --push; then
      fail=1
    fi
    ;;
esac

echo ""
echo "-- gate b: test suite green (scoped by the diff's reach, SPEC INV-45) --"
case "$reach_code" in
  0)
    echo "   prose-only diff: the suite stands down by name; every other gate still runs."
    ;;
  2)
    scoped_files="$(printf '%s\n' "$reach_out" | sed -n 's/^SCOPED //p')"
    if ! SCOPED_TEST_FILES="$scoped_files" "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
      fail=1
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-tests.sh"; then
      fail=1
    fi
    ;;
esac

echo ""
echo "-- gate c: every spec anchor owned by exactly one architecture node --"
echo "   Covered by gate b: tests/test_traceability.py already asserts this"
echo "   (test_architecture_owns_every_anchor_once) — no separate check needed here."

echo ""
echo "-- gate d: TEST_MATRIX.md generated Reference agrees with the body (SPEC INV-273/INV-218) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-matrix-reference.py" "$REPO_ROOT/TEST_MATRIX.md"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate g: pin drift --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-pin-drift.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate f: skill loadability --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-loadability.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate e: prototype fence --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-prototype-fence.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo "-- gate i: shipped-language (no owner name or stray Cyrillic in the shipped set, SPEC INV-120) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-shipped-language.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate j: no broad browser-kill (cleanup targets the test resource only, SPEC INV-162) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-broad-kill.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate l: muted browser launch (every browser-driving script launches muted, SPEC INV-157) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-muted-launch.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate o: cleanup notice (every cleanup path that ends a process says what it ended, SPEC INV-204) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-cleanup-notice.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate p: touchpoint kind (a surface speaks only the kind its touchpoint affords, SPEC INV-205) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-touchpoint-kind.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate q: waiting list (the board loses nothing — no over-cap shown set, no demotion into the void, SPEC INV-206) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-board.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate r: authority anchor (a decision recorded as the person's names its exchange, SPEC INV-207) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-authority-anchor.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate s: skill review (a substantive skill change carries its skill-creator review record, SPEC INV-208) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-skill-review.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate t: doc rotation (the pack's split-and-rotated docs lose nothing — every rotated row is findable in its archive and every archive is named in a manifest line, SPEC INV-209) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-doc-rotation.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate m: config health (installed hooks match guardrails/ source, SPEC INV-175) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-config-health.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate k: compaction freeze (guarded docs' anchor map / markers / numbers unchanged, 2.0) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-freeze.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate n: the earned message (an agent's inbox deposit names its birth, SPEC INV-189) --"
# Report-only at push (the owner's word, 2026-08-07 11:19): a deposit is recorded on arrival and
# never blocks a push. The check's judging moment is the intake sweep, which declines an unearned
# deposit at the door. Here it prints what the sweep will meet and the push proceeds either way.
if [ -f "$GUARDRAILS/check-earned-message.py" ] && [ -d "$REPO_ROOT/inbox" ]; then
  python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-earned-message.py" "$REPO_ROOT/inbox" || \
    echo "   (deposits above await the intake sweep; a deposit never blocks a push)"
else
  echo "   (no inbox in this tree — the gate stands down by name)"
fi

# The named-reference presence nets (SPEC INV-239) take NO push-gate letter and are NOT invoked here:
# they RIDE THE SUITE (gate b), the same placement the far-tier report-shape check takes. Their suite
# tests run each net against the real tree and assert the expected result, so a real violation reds
# the suite and gate b already blocks this push. A suite-riding check carries no gate letter, so the
# letter-counting meta-guards (INV-210, INV-212) need not see it and no gate-red-proofs / ci-mirror
# entry is owed.

echo ""
echo "-- gate h: the four host checks (this repo attached as its own first host, SPEC INV-97) --"
for hostcheck in completeness tests_present traces_to_spec conflicts; do
  if ! python3 "$REPO_ROOT/scaffold/guardrails/check_${hostcheck}.py" --base origin/main; then
    fail=1
  fi
done

echo ""
echo "-- gate u: CI mirror parity (every local gate is mirrored in CI or a declared carve-out, SPEC INV-210) --"
if ! "$GUARDRAILS/check-ci-mirror.sh"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate v: judges listed (every wired chat judge is referenced in the installed settings.json, SPEC INV-211) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-judge-listed.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate w: every gate can fail (every gate in this chain carries a known-red proof, SPEC INV-212) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-every-gate-can-fail.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate x: generated index (the committed index equals a fresh build off the body; body and index agree; an empty body reds by name, SPEC INV-258/INV-259/INV-218) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-index-generated.py" "$REPO_ROOT/PRODUCT_SPEC.md" "$REPO_ROOT/PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate y: agent card (a live-spec host tree carries its .live-spec/agent.md card, SPEC INV-219) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-agent-card.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate z: doc bound (each growable working doc within its declared bound or freshly rotated, SPEC INV-234) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-doc-bound.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate aa: doc findings bound (no live document above its recorded finding count; a cleared document stays at zero, SPEC INV-301) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-doc-findings-bound.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate ad: published tree counts (every count this repository publishes about its own tree matches the tree, and the reproduction command beside it returns the published number, SPEC INV-305) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-tree-counts.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
echo "-- gate ae: named checks (the registry says what each runnable file a skill body names is, SPEC INV-306) --"
if ! python3 "$GUARDRAILS/check-named-checks.py"; then
  fail=1
fi

echo ""
if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "PUSH BLOCKED — one or more gates above failed. Fix them and try again."
  exit 1
fi

# The gates are green, so this push is about to land — sync the standalone mirror repos
# from the pack now, so a mirror never drifts behind a shipped pack version again (a mirror
# was found one version behind on 2026-07-13). This runs ONLY past the blocked-push exit
# above, so a blocked push never reaches a mirror. It is NON-BLOCKING: a mirror hiccup
# (gh not authenticated, no network) warns and lets the pack push through — the CI arm and
# the next push both re-sync. Extends the push gate (SPEC M-6) and the mirror mechanism
# (scripts/sync-mirrors.sh, SPEC INV-96).
echo ""
echo "-- mirror sync (non-blocking) --"
if "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/sync-mirrors.sh"; then
  :
else
  echo "   warn: mirror sync did not complete (gh auth? network?) — run scripts/sync-mirrors.sh by hand."
fi

echo "All gates green — push allowed."
exit 0

133	# Tests pinned to ride EVERY scoped run, whatever the diff touched. Two kinds live here:
134	#   - an integrity rider: a test that must ride for the suite's own integrity whether or not it
135	#     enumerates infra dirs. tests/test_traceability.py is the first permanent member — the
136	#     traceability net rides every scoped verdict so a scoped run can never skip it.
137	#   - an enumerating-infra test: one that reads an infra directory by walk/glob rather than naming
138	#     basenames, invisible to the by-name discovery below, pinned here so it rides too.
139	# One home: the suite-hygiene net (tests/test_guardrails.py::TestScopedReachHygiene) reads THIS block

142	  "tests/test_traceability.py"      # integrity rider — rides every scoped run for suite integrity
143	  "tests/test_setup_entry.py"       # enumerating-infra test — globs skills/*/SKILL.md, invisible to by-name discovery
144	  "tests/test_guardrails_unit.py"   # the guardrail unit half: fast, sandbox-free, rides every scoped run
145	)
146	# SCOPED_EXCLUDED — test files the by-name discovery must NOT pull into a scoped run. One member:
147	# the guardrail integration half, whose classes copy the repository, build git sandboxes and run
148	# the suite inside the suite. It runs on explicit ask and in the full suite; a scoped run takes the
149	# unit half above instead. A changed infra file whose ONLY owning test sits in an excluded file
150	# counts as unowned and the diff falls to FULL — the conservative floor keeps its teeth.
151	SCOPED_EXCLUDED=(
152	  "tests/test_guardrails.py"
153	)
154	# --- ALWAYS_SCOPED (permanent scoped-run riders) END ---

156	scoped=()
157	scoped_has() {
158	  local needle="$1" x
159	  for x in "${scoped[@]:-}"; do
160	    [ "$x" = "$needle" ] && return 0
161	  done
162	  return 1
163	}

165	  # returns 1 (and adds nothing) for an excluded file, so a caller counting owners
166	  # never counts an excluded owner — the file then falls to FULL if nothing else owns it
167	  local ex
168	  for ex in "${SCOPED_EXCLUDED[@]:-}"; do
169	    [ -n "$ex" ] && [ "$1" = "$ex" ] && return 1
170	  done
171	  scoped_has "$1" || scoped+=("$1")
172	  return 0
173	}

175	conservative_full=0
176	for f in "${infra_files[@]}"; do
177	  case "$f" in
178	    tests/test_*.py)
179	      # a changed test file adds itself to the scoped set — it is its own owning test. A DELETED
180	      # test file must never be handed to pytest (a nonexistent path reds collection, a false red);
181	      # it falls through to by-name discovery and, unowned, to FULL [2.3.0 audit, finding 6].
182	      if [ -f "$f" ]; then
183	        if add_scoped "$f"; then
184	          continue
185	        fi
186	        # an excluded test file that itself changed falls through to by-name discovery
187	        # and, unowned there, to FULL
188	      fi
189	      ;;
190	  esac
191	
192	  base="$(basename "$f")"
193	  owning=0
194	
195	  while IFS= read -r t; do
196	    [ -z "$t" ] && continue
197	    if add_scoped "$t"; then
198	      owning=1
199	    fi
200	  done < <(grep -l -F -- "$base" tests/test_*.py 2>/dev/null || true)
201	
202	  while IFS= read -r r; do
203	    [ -z "$r" ] && continue
204	    [ "$r" = "$f" ] && continue
205	    rbase="$(basename "$r")"
206	    while IFS= read -r t; do
207	      [ -z "$t" ] && continue
208	      if add_scoped "$t"; then
209	        owning=1
210	      fi
211	    done < <(grep -l -F -- "$rbase" tests/test_*.py 2>/dev/null || true)
212	  done < <(grep -rl -F -- "$base" $REFERRER_DIRS 2>/dev/null || true)
213	
214	  if [ "$owning" -eq 0 ]; then
215	    echo "reach: '$f' names no test file (directly or via one referrer level) — conservative fall-through to FULL."
216	    conservative_full=1
217	  fi
218	done
219	
220	if [ "$conservative_full" -ne 0 ]; then
221	  exit 1
222	fi
223	
224	for t in "${ALWAYS_SCOPED[@]:-}"; do
225	  [ -z "$t" ] && continue
226	  if [ ! -f "$t" ]; then
227	    # a stale pin must red loudly under its own name here, never as a bare pytest collection error
228	    echo "BLOCK (reach): ALWAYS_SCOPED pins a missing file: $t — fix the pin before pushing." >&2
229	    exit 1
230	  fi
231	  add_scoped "$t" || true
232	done
233	
234	sorted_scoped="$(printf '%s\n' "${scoped[@]}" | sort -u)"
235	printf '%s\n' "$sorted_scoped" | while IFS= read -r t; do
236	  [ -z "$t" ] && continue
237	  echo "SCOPED $t"
238	done
239	count="$(printf '%s\n' "$sorted_scoped" | grep -c .)"
240	echo "OK (reach): infra-class diff — scoped to $count test files (each names a changed file; + the traceability net), SPEC INV-45"
241	exit 2

# tests are found mechanically by filename — grep for the changed file's basename over tests/test_*.py
# — plus ONE referrer level: a file under one of the infra dirs that names the changed file's basename

# rider. A changed infra file that no test names (directly or via a referrer) is not

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

BASE="${1:-origin/main}"

# file into are the HOST's to declare, not this script's to hold as constants: they are read

# — declares its own classes there once (the same knowledge project.layers carries, SPEC

  # the key is absent or unreadable (which lands on the conservative floor above).
  python3 - "$CONFIG" "$1" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null || true
import json, sys
try:
    with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
        cfg = json.load(f)
except Exception:
    sys.exit(0)
for v in cfg.get("reach_classes", {}).get(sys.argv[2], []):
    print(v)
PY
}

PROSE_DIRS=();  while IFS= read -r x; do [ -n "$x" ] && PROSE_DIRS+=("$x");  done < <(reach_class prose_dirs)
INFRA_DIRS=();  while IFS= read -r x; do [ -n "$x" ] && INFRA_DIRS+=("$x");  done < <(reach_class infra_dirs)
INFRA_FILES=(); while IFS= read -r x; do [ -n "$x" ] && INFRA_FILES+=("$x"); done < <(reach_class infra_files)
INFRA_GLOBS=(); while IFS= read -r x; do [ -n "$x" ] && INFRA_GLOBS+=("$x"); done < <(reach_class infra_globs)

else

    echo "reach: base ref '$BASE' not found — conservative fall-through to FULL."
    exit 1

fi

matches_prose() {
  local f="$1" p
  for p in "${PROSE_FILES[@]:-}"; do [ -z "$p" ] && continue; [ "$f" = "$p" ] && return 0; done
  for p in "${PROSE_DIRS[@]:-}"; do [ -z "$p" ] && continue; case "$f" in "$p"/*) return 0 ;; esac; done
  return 1
}

matches_infra() {
  local f="$1" p
  for p in "${INFRA_FILES[@]:-}"; do [ -z "$p" ] && continue; [ "$f" = "$p" ] && return 0; done
  for p in "${INFRA_DIRS[@]:-}"; do [ -z "$p" ] && continue; case "$f" in "$p"/*) return 0 ;; esac; done
  for p in "${INFRA_GLOBS[@]:-}"; do [ -z "$p" ] && continue; case "$f" in $p) return 0 ;; esac; done
  return 1
}

full=0
infra_files=()

    continue
  elif matches_infra "$f"; then
    infra_files+=("$f")
  else
    echo "reach: '$f' is outside the prose/infra classes — FULL suite."
    full=1
  fi
done <<< "$files"

  echo "reach: empty diff — conservative fall-through to FULL."
  exit 1
fi

  exit 1
fi

  exit 0

#   - an integrity rider: a test that must ride for the suite's own integrity whether or not it
#     enumerates infra dirs. tests/test_traceability.py is the first permanent member — the
#     traceability net rides every scoped verdict so a scoped run can never skip it.
#   - an enumerating-infra test: one that reads an infra directory by walk/glob rather than naming
#     basenames, invisible to the by-name discovery below, pinned here so it rides too.
# One home: the suite-hygiene net (tests/test_guardrails.py::TestScopedReachHygiene) reads THIS block
# [ROADMAP 366].

  "tests/test_traceability.py"      # integrity rider — rides every scoped run for suite integrity
  "tests/test_setup_entry.py"       # enumerating-infra test — globs skills/*/SKILL.md, invisible to by-name discovery
  "tests/test_guardrails_unit.py"   # the guardrail unit half: fast, sandbox-free, rides every scoped run

# the guardrail integration half, whose classes copy the repository, build git sandboxes and run
# the suite inside the suite. It runs on explicit ask and in the full suite; a scoped run takes the
# unit half above instead. A changed infra file whose ONLY owning test sits in an excluded file
# counts as unowned and the diff falls to FULL — the conservative floor keeps its teeth.
SCOPED_EXCLUDED=(

)
# --- ALWAYS_SCOPED (permanent scoped-run riders) END ---

scoped_has() {
  local needle="$1" x
  for x in "${scoped[@]:-}"; do
    [ "$x" = "$needle" ] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}
add_scoped() {
  # returns 1 (and adds nothing) for an excluded file, so a caller counting owners
  # never counts an excluded owner — the file then falls to FULL if nothing else owns it
  local ex
  for ex in "${SCOPED_EXCLUDED[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$ex" ] && [ "$1" = "$ex" ] && return 1
  done
  scoped_has "$1" || scoped+=("$1")
  return 0
}

conservative_full=0
for f in "${infra_files[@]}"; do
  case "$f" in
    tests/test_*.py)
      # a changed test file adds itself to the scoped set — it is its own owning test. A DELETED
      # test file must never be handed to pytest (a nonexistent path reds collection, a false red);
      # it falls through to by-name discovery and, unowned, to FULL [2.3.0 audit, finding 6].
      if [ -f "$f" ]; then
        if add_scoped "$f"; then
          continue
        fi
        # an excluded test file that itself changed falls through to by-name discovery
        # and, unowned there, to FULL
      fi
      ;;
  esac

  base="$(basename "$f")"
  owning=0

  while IFS= read -r t; do
    [ -z "$t" ] && continue
    if add_scoped "$t"; then
      owning=1
    fi
  done < <(grep -l -F -- "$base" tests/test_*.py 2>/dev/null || true)

  while IFS= read -r r; do
    [ -z "$r" ] && continue
    [ "$r" = "$f" ] && continue
    rbase="$(basename "$r")"
    while IFS= read -r t; do
      [ -z "$t" ] && continue
      if add_scoped "$t"; then
        owning=1
      fi
    done < <(grep -l -F -- "$rbase" tests/test_*.py 2>/dev/null || true)

    echo "reach: '$f' names no test file (directly or via one referrer level) — conservative fall-through to FULL."
    conservative_full=1
  fi
done

if [ "$conservative_full" -ne 0 ]; then
  exit 1
fi

  [ -z "$t" ] && continue
  if [ ! -f "$t" ]; then
    # a stale pin must red loudly under its own name here, never as a bare pytest collection error
    echo "BLOCK (reach): ALWAYS_SCOPED pins a missing file: $t — fix the pin before pushing." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  add_scoped "$t" || true
done

printf '%s\n' "$sorted_scoped" | while IFS= read -r t; do
  [ -z "$t" ] && continue
  echo "SCOPED $t"
done
count="$(printf '%s\n' "$sorted_scoped" | grep -c .)"
echo "OK (reach): infra-class diff — scoped to $count test files (each names a changed file; + the traceability net), SPEC INV-45"
exit 2

content.content:
# newest commit touching PRODUCT_SPEC.md, and separately at least as new as the newest commit
# touching ARCHITECTURE.md (equal, or the document's commit is an ancestor of the record's
# commit — a record may ship in the very same commit as the document change it covers).

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

# Two roads (row 571, the cost audit's repair b). The PUSH road (--push; pre-push and CI pass
# it) keeps the original demand: a record dated today. The default WORK road serves an ordinary
# suite run: a clean tree after midnight is not a defect, so it also accepts the newest committed
# record of any date — the freshness checks below still refuse it the moment PRODUCT_SPEC.md or
# ARCHITECTURE.md changed after it.
PUSH_ROAD=0
if [ "${1:-}" = "--push" ]; then
  PUSH_ROAD=1
  shift
fi

PROVER_DIR="${1:-docs/prover}"
TODAY="${2:-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)}"

# Carve-out (row 269, SPEC M-6/INV-112): a push whose diff is exactly one NEW file under
# inbox/ — the remote-deposit shape — changes no spec-backed content, so it owes no fresh
# prover record. This mirrors the spec-level carve-out into the gate script, so an inbox
# deposit on a day with no committed record does not red the CI. A diff carrying anything
# more (a second file, an edit, a delete) rides the full gate below.
#   The diff is measured against a BASE ref: LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE if set (CI passes
#   github.event.before, a planted test passes the base commit), else origin/main, else
#   HEAD~1. If no base resolves, the carve-out cannot be judged and the full gate runs.
DIFF_BASE=""
if [ -n "${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE:-}" ] && \
   [ "${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE}" != "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ] && \
   git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE}^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  DIFF_BASE="${LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE}"
elif git rev-parse --verify --quiet origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  DIFF_BASE="origin/main"
elif git rev-parse --verify --quiet "HEAD~1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  DIFF_BASE="HEAD~1"
fi

if [ -n "$DIFF_BASE" ]; then
  changed="$(git diff --name-status "$DIFF_BASE" HEAD)"
  # exactly one line, status A (added), path under inbox/
  if [ "$(printf '%s' "$changed" | grep -c '')" -eq 1 ] && \
     printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep -qE '^A[[:space:]]+inbox/'; then
    echo "OK (prover record): carve-out — the pushed diff is exactly one new inbox/ file"
    echo "  (the remote-deposit shape, SPEC M-6/INV-112); no fresh prover record is owed."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

shopt -s nullglob
candidates=("$PROVER_DIR"/"$TODAY"*.md)
shopt -u nullglob
